question: 「せいぜい」の意味はなんですか。
source_explanation:
せいぜい means 'at most' — indicating the maximum limit of something, usually a small or disappointing one.
せいぜい is an adverb meaning 'at most,' 'at best,' or 'no more than.' It describes an upper limit that is typically lower than expected or hoped for. せいぜい百人 (ひゃくにん) = at most a hundred people. It often carries a slightly deflating tone — the number or amount is limited and probably less than you would want. せいぜい〜ても = 'even at best, even if you do the most you can.' 彼女にできることは、せいぜい連絡することくらいだ (the most she can do is contact them). It is written in hiragana and does not have a standard kanji form.

question: 「少なくとも」の意味はなんですか。
source_explanation:
少なくとも means 'at least' — setting a lower bound on a quantity or condition.
少なくとも (すくなくとも) is an adverb meaning 'at least.' It sets a minimum: 「少なくとも３時間は必要です」 means 'at least three hours are necessary.' The word is built from 少ない (すくない, few/little) + 少なく (conjunctive form) + とも (a particle meaning 'even at the least'). Together: 'even taking the smallest number, it is still X.' 少なくとも appears in both formal writing and natural speech. Its antonym is せいぜい (at most), and the two are common pair on N3 vocabulary tests.
✗ Exactly is ちょうど or きっかり. 少なくとも sets a floor (minimum), not a precise figure.

question: 「接続」の読み方はなんですか。
source_explanation:
接続 is read せつぞく and means 'connection' — linking things together.
接続 (せつぞく) is a noun and する-verb meaning 'to connect,' 'to link,' or 'to join.' Both kanji use their on-yomi: 接 (せつ) and 続 (ぞく). 接 means 'to touch,' 'to join,' or 'to contact' — as in 接触 (せっしょく, contact) and 接続詞 (せつぞくし, conjunction in grammar). 続 means 'to continue' or 'to follow on' — as in 続く (つづく, to continue) and 継続 (けいぞく, continuation). Together, 接続 describes joining two things so they flow together — most commonly used for network connections (インターネット接続, internet connection) and logical connectors in grammar.

source_explanation:
せいぜい and 少なくとも are opposites — one sets an upper limit, the other a lower limit.
せいぜい means 'at most / at best' — it sets an upper ceiling on what is possible. 少なくとも (すくなくとも) means 'at least' — it sets a lower floor. They are opposite in direction. せいぜい百人 (hyakunin) しか来ない = 'At most only a hundred people will come.' 少なくとも百人は来る = 'At least a hundred people will come.' The same number, but せいぜい says the ceiling is there; 少なくとも says the floor is there. These two adverbs work on opposite ends of a range: せいぜい caps the estimate low; 少なくとも anchors the estimate high. 接続 (せつぞく) means 'connection / to connect.' 接 (せつ) means 'to touch / to join,' and 続 (ぞく) means 'to continue / to follow.' Together they describe the act of joining one thing to another in sequence — a network connection, a cable plugged in, or a session link. インターネットに接続する is the standard phrase for 'to connect to the internet.' The sentence says: 「インターネットに（ ）できません」 — 'I cannot ( ) to the internet.' 接続 fits perfectly. Notice the particle に: 接続する always takes に to mark what you are connecting to.

question: 「該当」の読み方はなんですか。
source_explanation:
該当 is read がいとう and means 'to apply to / to be applicable' or 'the relevant item.'
該当 (がいとう) is an on-yomi compound meaning 'to be applicable,' 'to correspond to,' or 'the relevant case/item.' 該 (がい) means 'that very / applicable,' and 当 (とう) means 'to hit the mark / to apply to.' Together they describe the situation where something matches a criterion or applies to a given category. 該当する means 'to apply / to qualify': 条件 (じょうけん) に該当する (to meet the conditions), 該当なし (がいとうなし, not applicable / N/A). question: 「該当する項目」の意味はなんですか。
source_explanation:
該当する項目 means 'applicable items' — the items that satisfy a given condition.
該当 (がいとう) is a noun and する-verb meaning 'to apply to,' 'to correspond to,' or 'to be applicable.' 項目 (こうもく) means 'item,' 'entry,' or 'category.' Together, 該当する項目 refers to items that meet a stated condition. On Japanese forms, 「該当する項目にチェックを入れてください」 (please check the applicable items) is standard. 該当 is formal and appears in official documents, government forms, and legal texts. question: 「頻繁」の読み方はなんですか。
source_explanation:
頻繁 is read ひんぱん and means 'frequent' or 'repeated at short intervals.'
頻繁 (ひんぱん) is a な-adjective / adverb meaning 'frequent,' 'repeated many times,' or 'occurring at short intervals.' 頻 (ひん) means 'frequent / repeated,' and 繁 (はん) means 'flourishing / dense / busy.' Together they describe something that happens often and in rapid succession. 頻繁に連絡 (れんらく) する means 'to contact frequently'; 頻繁な会議 (かいぎ) means 'frequent meetings.' question: 「頻繁に」の意味はなんですか。
source_explanation:
頻繁に (ひんぱんに) means 'frequently' — happening often, at short intervals.
頻繁に (ひんぱんに) is the adverbial form of the な-adjective 頻繁 (ひんぱん), meaning 'frequent.' It describes something that happens repeatedly and at short intervals. 頻繁に連絡する (れんらくする) = to contact frequently; 頻繁に使われる表現 (ひょうげん) = an expression used frequently. At N3, this word appears in formal writing, business communication, and academic contexts. question: 「順調」の読み方はなんですか。
source_explanation:
順調 is read じゅんちょう and means 'going smoothly / without problems.'
順調 (じゅんちょう) is a na-adjective meaning 'smooth progress,' 'going well,' or 'without obstacles.' 順 (じゅん) means 'in order / sequential / smooth,' and 調 (ちょう) means 'condition / tune / adjustment.' Together they describe a state where things proceed exactly as planned, with nothing derailing the process. 工事 (こうじ) が順調に進む (construction proceeds smoothly), 回復 (かいふく) が順調 (recovery is going well), 計画 (けいかく) は順調に実施されている (the plan is being implemented smoothly). All three options describe things going well: 快調 (かいちょう) = 'in fine form / running smoothly,' often used for engines, health, and momentum. 好調 (こうちょう) = 'in good condition / performing well,' frequently used in sports, sales, and business. 順調 (じゅんちょう) = 'going smoothly / without problems,' the most general of the three for steady progress. question: 「ひたすら」の意味はなんですか。
source_explanation:
ひたすら means 'earnestly' or 'solely' — single-mindedly focused on one thing without distraction.
ひたすら is an adverb meaning 'solely,' 'single-mindedly,' 'earnestly,' or 'with undivided focus.' It describes someone who does only one thing with complete dedication, excluding all other considerations. 「ひたすら努力 (どりょく) する」= 'to work single-mindedly at something.' 「ひたすら待 (ま) つ」= 'to simply wait, doing nothing else.' question: 薬を飲んだが、（＿＿＿）悪くなった。

The sentence says 'I took medicine, but I got ( ) worse.' The expected outcome of taking medicine is improvement; かえって signals that the actual outcome went the opposite way — things got worse instead of better. question: 「見積もり」の意味はなんですか。
source_explanation:
見積もり (みつもり) means 'estimate' or 'quote' — a calculated projection of cost, time, or quantity.
見積もり (みつもり) is a noun meaning 'estimate,' 'quote,' or 'projected cost.' It comes from the verb 見積もる (みつもる, to estimate / to calculate in advance). 見 (み) means 'to look / see,' and 積 (もる/つもる) means 'to pile up / to calculate.' Together they suggest a careful, advance calculation. In business Japanese, 見積もりを取る means 'to get a quote' (from a contractor or supplier), and 見積もりを出す means 'to give an estimate.' question: 「締結」の読み方はなんですか。
source_explanation:
締結 is read ていけつ and means 'conclusion / signing (of a contract or agreement).'
締結 (ていけつ) is a formal noun meaning 'conclusion' or 'signing' — specifically of a contract, treaty, or agreement. 締 (てい) means 'to close / to tighten,' and 結 (けつ) means 'to bind / to conclude.' Together they describe the act of formally sealing an agreement by closing and binding it. 条約 (じょうやく) の締結 (conclusion of a treaty), 契約 (けいやく) を締結する (to sign a contract). This word belongs to formal legal and diplomatic language. The reading ていけつ uses on-yomi for both characters: 締 (てい) and 結 (けつ).

question: 「解除」の読み方はなんですか。
source_explanation:
解除 is read かいじょ and means 'cancellation / removal / lifting (of a restriction).'
解除 (かいじょ) is a noun meaning 'cancellation,' 'removal,' or 'lifting' — taking away a lock, restriction, contract, or state of emergency. 解 (かい) means 'to undo / to release,' and 除 (じょ) means 'to remove / to eliminate.' question: 「採用」の読み方はなんですか。
source_explanation:
採用 is read さいよう and means 'hiring' or 'adoption of a plan/method.'
採用 (さいよう) is a noun and する-verb meaning either (1) hiring someone for a position — 人を採用する (ひとをさいようする) — or (2) adopting or accepting a plan, method, or idea — 方針を採用する (ほうしんをさいようする). Both kanji use their on-yomi: 採 (さい) and 用 (よう). 採 means 'to pick' or 'to select' — as in 採点 (さいてん, scoring) and 採取 (さいしゅ, sampling). 用 means 'use,' 'function,' or 'employment' — as in 使用 (しよう, usage) and 活用 (かつよう, utilization). question: 新しい社員を（＿＿＿）しました。
source_explanation:
採用 (さいよう) fits because the sentence is about hiring a new employee.
採用 (さいよう) means 'to hire / to adopt / to take on.' 採 (さい) means 'to select / to pick,' and 用 (よう) means 'to use / to employ.' Together they describe selecting someone (or something) to put into use. 新しい社員を採用する (to hire a new employee) is a natural and common expression. 採用 also applies to adopting ideas or systems: 新しい方法を採用する (to adopt a new method). In the HR context, 採用 is the entire hiring process: 採用試験 (さいようしけん, hiring exam), 採用通知 (さいようつうち, offer letter). The sentence says: 「新しい社員を（ ）しました」 — 'We ( ) a new employee.'

question: 「解雇」の読み方はなんですか。
source_explanation:
解雇 is read かいこ and means 'dismissal from employment' — being fired or let go.
解雇 (かいこ) is the formal word for terminating an employee's employment. 解 (かい) has the on-yomi かい and means 'to undo' or 'to dissolve'; it appears in 解決 (かいけつ, resolution), 解散 (かいさん, dissolution), and 解放 (かいほう, liberation). 雇 (こ) has the on-yomi こ and means 'to employ' or 'to hire'; it appears in 雇用 (こよう, employment). question: 「昇進」の読み方はなんですか。
source_explanation:
昇進 is read しょうしん and means 'promotion (in rank or job title).'
昇進 (しょうしん) is a noun and する-verb meaning 'to be promoted' at work or in an organization. Both kanji use their on-yomi: 昇 (しょう) and 進 (しん). 昇 means 'to rise' — as in 上昇 (じょうしょう, rise/increase) and 昇格 (しょうかく, upgrade in status). 進 means 'to advance' — as in 進歩 (しんぽ, progress) and 進学 (しんがく, advancing to higher education). Together, 昇進 literally means 'rising and advancing.' In business Japanese: 課長に昇進した (かちょうにしょうしんした, was promoted to section chief). The register is formal.

question: 「降格」の意味はなんですか。
source_explanation:
降格 (こうかく) means 'demotion' — being moved to a lower rank or position.
降格 (こうかく) is the formal word for a reduction in rank or grade. 降 (こう) means 'to descend' or 'to lower'; its kun-yomi おり appears in 降りる (おりる, to get off/descend). 格 (かく) means 'rank,' 'status,' or 'grade'; it appears in 資格 (しかく, qualification), 合格 (ごうかく, passing an exam), and 格差 (かくさ, disparity). Together: こうかく = 'moving down in rank' = demotion. The opposite is 昇格 (しょうかく, promotion in rank). In the workplace, 降格処分 (こうかくしょぶん) means 'disciplinary demotion.' Both kanji use their on-yomi.

question: 「かろうじて」の意味はなんですか。
source_explanation:
かろうじて means 'barely / narrowly' — succeeding (or surviving) by the smallest margin.
かろうじて is an adverb meaning 'barely,' 'narrowly,' or 'just barely.' It describes a situation where something was achieved or avoided only by the tiniest margin — close enough that failure was a real possibility. かろうじて合格 (ごうかく) した (barely passed), かろうじて間 (ま) に合 (あ) った (just barely made it in time), かろうじて命 (いのち) を取 (と) り留 (と) めた (narrowly survived). question: 「辞任」の読み方はなんですか。
source_explanation:
辞任 is read じにん and means 'resignation from a position.'
辞任 (じにん) is an on-yomi compound. 辞 (じ) means 'to resign / to leave a post,' and 任 (にん) means 'duty / appointment / post.' Together they describe the act of voluntarily stepping down from a position of responsibility — a minister resigning, a CEO stepping down, a committee chair leaving their role. 辞任する means 'to resign.' question: 「たちまち」の意味はなんですか。
source_explanation:
たちまち means 'in an instant' — something happening so fast it seems almost simultaneous.
たちまち is an adverb meaning 'in an instant,' 'immediately,' or 'in no time at all.' It describes how quickly something happens or changes, often with a sense of surprise at the speed. Written in kanji, it can appear as 忽ち, but modern Japanese almost always uses hiragana. question: 「いきなり」の意味はなんですか。
source_explanation:
いきなり means 'suddenly / abruptly' — without any warning or transition.
いきなり is an adverb meaning 'suddenly,' 'abruptly,' or 'without warning.' question: 「いちいち」の意味はなんですか。
source_explanation:
いちいち means 'one by one' or 'every single [thing]' — attending to or mentioning each item individually.
いちいち is an adverb meaning 'one by one,' 'each and every,' or 'in every individual case.' It comes from 一一 (いちいち, one by one), though it is nearly always written in hiragana today. question: 「思わず」の意味はなんですか。
source_explanation:
思わず means 'involuntarily / unintentionally' — doing something without meaning to.
思わず (おもわず) is an adverb meaning 'involuntarily,' 'without thinking,' or 'unintentionally.' It is built from 思う (おもう, to think/intend) + the negative auxiliary わず (an older classical form of ない). question: 「案の定」の意味はなんですか。
source_explanation:
案の定 (あんのじょう) means 'as expected' — something turned out exactly the way you predicted.
案の定 (あんのじょう) is an adverbial set phrase meaning 'as expected,' 'just as I thought,' or 'sure enough.' 案 (あん) means 'idea / plan / prediction,' and 定 (じょう) means 'fixed / settled / confirmed.' question: 「あくまで」の意味はなんですか。
source_explanation:
あくまで means 'to the end / stubbornly' — holding firmly to a position no matter what.
あくまで (飽くまで) is an adverb meaning 'to the very end,' 'stubbornly,' or 'under all circumstances.' It describes a determination that does not budge regardless of opposition or difficulty. question: 「かえって」の意味はなんですか。
source_explanation:
かえって means 'on the contrary / the opposite effect' — when an action produces the reverse of what was intended.
かえって is an adverb meaning 'on the contrary,' 'contrary to expectations,' or 'the opposite happened.' question: 「就任」の読み方はなんですか。
source_explanation:
就任 is read しゅうにん and means 'taking up / assuming a (official) post.'
就任 (しゅうにん) is a formal noun meaning 'assuming a post' or 'taking office.' 就 (しゅう) means 'to settle into / to take up,' and 任 (にん) means 'duty / appointment.' question: 「辛うじて」の意味はなんですか。
source_explanation:
辛うじて (からうじて) means 'barely' or 'narrowly' — succeeding only by the smallest margin.
辛うじて (からうじて) is an adverb meaning 'barely,' 'narrowly,' 'just barely,' or 'by the skin of one's teeth.' It describes an outcome where success was achieved only with the smallest possible margin — nearly failing, but managing to succeed at the last moment. The kanji 辛 (から/しん) means 'difficult' or 'painful'; the compound 辛うじて carries the image of forcing through something painful with just enough effort. question: 「とりわけ」の意味はなんですか。
source_explanation:
とりわけ means 'especially / particularly' — singling out one item as more notable than the rest.
とりわけ is an adverb meaning 'especially,' 'particularly,' or 'above all.' It is used to single out one item from a group and emphasize that it stands apart. とりわけ好きな食べ物は寿司だ (What I especially like is sushi). It is a more formal and literary equivalent of 特に (とくに), which is the most common everyday word for 'especially.' とりわけ is written in hiragana and is more common in written Japanese than in conversation. question: 「さほど」の意味はなんですか。（否定文で）
source_explanation:
さほど (in a negative sentence) means 'not so much' — the degree is less than expected.
さほど is an adverb meaning 'to that extent' or 'so much,' and it almost always appears in a negative sentence: さほど〜ない = 'not particularly,' 'not that much,' 'not so [adjective].' For example: 「さほど難 (むずか) しくない」= 'not particularly difficult'; 「さほど気 (き) にならない」= 'I don't really mind.' question: 「漠然」の読み方はなんですか。
source_explanation:
漠然 is read ばくぜん and means 'vague' or 'hazy.'
漠然 (ばくぜん) is read with its on-yomi: 漠 (ばく) and 然 (ぜん). 漠 (ばく) means 'vast and empty' or 'unclear' — the image of a huge featureless expanse like a desert. 然 (ぜん/ねん) is a suffix-like character meaning 'in such a state' or 'naturally so' — appearing in many Japanese adverbs: 当然 (とうぜん, naturally), 突然 (とつぜん, suddenly), 全然 (ぜんぜん, not at all). Together, 漠然 describes a state of being indistinct or lacking definition. The compound is nearly always followed by と or とした: 漠然と感じる (ばくぜんとかんじる, feel vaguely), 漠然とした不安 (ばくぜんとしたふあん, vague anxiety).

question: 「網羅的」の意味はなんですか。

question: 「端的」の読み方はなんですか。

question: 「余儀なくされる」の意味はなんですか。
source_explanation:
余儀なくされる (よぎなくされる) means 'to be forced to / compelled to do something' by circumstances beyond one's control.

question: 「顕著」の読み方はなんですか。
source_explanation:
顕著 is read けんちょ and means 'remarkable' or 'conspicuous.'
顕著 (けんちょ) is a formal on-yomi compound. 顕 (けん) means 'to become visible / to stand out,' and 著 (ちょ) means 'remarkable / striking / notable.'
